transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

The fact that it iced up again just two weeks after a manual defrost suggests an automatic defrost fault. In a frost-free appliance, a heater and thermostat work together to melt ice off the coils every few hours. If one of these fails (or the control board doesn't trigger them), ice builds up on the evaporator coil behind the rear panel. This blockage stops cold air from circulating properly into the fridge section and can cause excess moisture to freeze in the drawers, making them jam. While a blocked drain could also cause water/ice issues, the rapid re-icing points more towards the defrost system not running at all. To narrow this down, I need you to do one check: switch the appliance off and let it fully defrost (remove any food to cool bags). Once it's clear of ice, look behind the rear panel inside the freezer. 1. Is the metal coil/finning covered in a solid block of ice?
2. Is there water pooling at the bottom of the cabinet? Please let me know what you see when you open it up.
its not frost free tho, its a normal manual defrost freezer so no heater or rear panel as far as i know. its only 2wks since i defrosted it. what else could cause it?

You're right to correct me—if it's a manual defrost model, there is no automatic heater or timer to fail. The rapid re-icing (within two weeks) usually points to one of two things: either the door seal isn't keeping warm air out, or the internal drain for condensation water is blocked. If warm air gets past the seal, it brings in moisture that freezes instantly on the cold surfaces. If the drain is blocked, melting ice (from normal operation) has nowhere to go and pools at the bottom, freezing into a block that stops the drawer from closing. To sort this out safely, please switch the appliance off and let it fully defrost completely—remove food to cool bags, put towels down, and leave doors open for about 24 hours. Once it's clear:
1. Check the rubber door seal for any tears, gaps, or sections that have come away from the frame.
2. Look at the bottom of the back wall inside the freezer/fridge section to see if there is a small drain hole and whether it looks blocked with ice or debris. Let me know what you find with the seal first.

looked at the seal, bottom corner of the freezer door seal is split about 5cm and the hinge-side bottom bit is flattened. not sure about the drain hole tbh, didnt see one. is the seal the problem then?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Yes, that seal is probably the problem. The fix is to replace that rubber seal. To make sure we get the right part for your Indesit fridge-freezer, I need the model number. It’s usually on a sticker inside the appliance, often on a side wall near the salad drawer or on the door frame. Can you find it and read it out?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok its IB55532W, indesit. whats the seal called to search for, and is it push in or screwed? i can fit it myself

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That split and flattened section is most likely the problem. Warm air from your kitchen is getting in through that gap, hitting the cold surfaces, and turning into ice very quickly—hence why it iced up again so fast after you defrosted it. Regarding the part: for an Indesit IB55532W, this is called a 'freezer door seal' or 'gasket'. Most Indesit seals of this era are held in by a plastic retaining strip that clips into a groove around the edge of the door. You don't need screws; you just unclip the old one and press the new one (and its retaining strip) into place. Because I cannot verify the exact seal profile for your specific model number against the parts catalogue, I strongly recommend ordering from Indesit's official online spare parts store or a major UK retailer using your model number IB55532W. This ensures you get the correct shape and clip type. 1. Ensure the freezer is completely dry and defrosted (as discussed).
2. Clean the groove on the door with warm soapy water to remove any old adhesive or debris.
3. Once fitted, close the door gently to check it seals properly. If you find the seal doesn't quite match or the door alignment is off after fitting, that's when a qualified engineer might be needed to adjust the hinges, but for most people, replacing the seal resolves this icing issue completely.
